id: title:DanielVisca:name the nesting mistake when a required object param is flattened

observations.behavior: Adds unwrapped-payload detection before returning generic missing-parameter messages.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies MCP agent error responses when callers send flattened parameters instead of nested objects.

observations.code_quote: const message = formatInputValidationError(tool.name, validation.error, input, tool.schema)
observations.behavior: Passes raw input and the Zod schema to the formatting function for disambiguation. No other hunks change this call site's arguments or behavior; P1.F1 only changes a different invocation without supplying these new optional args, leaving it unchanged rather than broken.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes how PostHog’s MCP-compatible tools communicate failure reasons back to agents using those tools.

observations.behavior: Adds tests asserting that specific wrapped-input cases receive nesting instructions while empty/undeclared-key inputs do not. No production implementation is changed here; this hunk adds checks against the already-present logic in P1.F2.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection for the improved error messaging added earlier.

observations.limitations: The tier depends on whether the broader MCP integration relies heavily on parameter parsing and user-facing diagnostics. The patch does not show adoption metrics, incident avoidance, or systemic architectural dependency. Tests are present but could still leave edge cases unverified if future implementations omit unwrapped-payload handling. No score can account for potential benefit beyond what the code demonstrates: clearer messages, no wider capability, no risk reduction across unrelated components.

review.reason: Substantive bounded improvement: better diagnostic clarity for a shared tool-execution path with supporting implementation and targeted tests. Not Tier 3 because there is no evidence of broader system-wide impact or critical-path coverage. Not Tier 1 because the change improves behavior and includes relevant checks rather than being purely maintenance or documentation.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog’s public MCP-compatible agent interfaces; helps users and agents understand why certain requests fail without changing ingestion, storage, or query execution.
review.uncertainty: Could be higher-tier only if this pattern dominates many tools and failures were previously ambiguous enough to cause repeated retries or support tickets; that cannot be established from this chunk alone.
